title: Blatant calibration cases, subtle live faults
statement: Does a calibration set built from blatant faults show that a judge will catch the subtle faults that actually occur?
example: Seven of one AP judge's 15 failing calibration cases expect a cognitive-demand failure, six of them for asking only for recall.
detail: An AP judge's calibration set holds 25 cases, 23 of them multiple choice, and its 15 failing cases are mostly blatant: seven expect a cognitive-demand failure, two absolute language, one a structural fault, two gross period misplacements and three factual errors, one of them subtle (1832 for 1830) (`APinceptbench/ap_benchmark/calibration/gold_standard.json`). In a live run, factual accuracy became the commonest failing dimension, with 24 failures whose patterns were events placed in the wrong period, geographic slips and oversimplifications (`APinceptbench/docs/reports/BENCHMARK_RUN2_REPORT.md`). Whether catching the first kind predicts catching the second has not been measured.
